questions.question: My friends play ___ badminton every evening.
questions.explanation: Names of sports generally take no article.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Names of games such as chess generally take no article when referring to the activity.

questions.question: The children go to ___ school every morning.
questions.explanation: Go to school without an article refers to attending school as students.

questions.question: His grandfather is in ___ hospital for treatment.
questions.explanation: In British and Indian English, 'in hospital' can refer to being there as a patient. In American English, 'in the hospital' is more common.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: He goes to the bed early.
He goes to a bed early.
He goes to an bed early.
questions.explanation: Go to bed without an article refers to the ordinary activity of sleeping.

questions.question: They played ___ football after school.
questions.explanation: Names of sports generally take no article.

questions.question: The suspect was taken to ___ prison.
questions.explanation: Taken to prison without an article refers to being imprisoned, not merely taken to a particular building.

questions.question: Which sentence refers to a particular building?
options: She goes to school every day.
I went to the school to meet the principal.
questions.correctAnswer: I went to the school to meet the principal.
questions.explanation: The school identifies a particular building visited for a purpose other than attending lessons as a student.

questions.question: My brother plays ___ hockey professionally.
questions.explanation: Names of sports generally do not take an article.

questions.question: The patient was taken to ___ hospital near our house.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'near our house' identifies a particular hospital building.

questions.question: Which expression is correct?
options: go to the church for worship
go to a church for worship in the institutional sense
go to an church for worship
questions.explanation: Church without an article can refer to attending religious services. 'The church' refers to a particular building.

questions.question: She is learning to play ___ golf.
questions.explanation: Names of sports generally take no article.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The prisoners are in a prison as an institution.
The prisoners are in an prison.
The prisoners are in prison in a general institutional sense.
questions.correctAnswer: The prisoners are in prison in a general institutional sense.
questions.explanation: The institutional expression 'in prison' takes no article. 'In a prison' or 'in the prison' refers to a particular prison or building.

questions.question: He goes to ___ university to study engineering.
questions.explanation: In British and Indian English, 'go to university' can refer to attending university as a student. 'The university' identifies a particular institution.

questions.question: Which sentence uses zero article correctly?
options: They play the volleyball on Sundays.
They play a volleyball on Sundays.
They play an volleyball on Sundays.
questions.explanation: Names of sports generally take no article when referring to the activity.

questions.question: The visitors went to ___ school to attend the annual function.
questions.explanation: The school refers to a particular building visited by the visitors for an event, not attending school as students.
